claims.quote: A Scheme number is exact if it was written as an exact constant or was derived from exact numbers using only exact operations.
Scheme explicitly distinguishes exact from inexact numbers.
If two implementations produce exact results for a computation that did not involve inexact intermediate results, the two ultimate results will be mathematically equal.

says.covers: results that are mathematically exact

claims.quote: This is generally not true of computations involving inexact numbers since approximate methods such as floating-point arithmetic may be used

says.covers: results that are mathematically exact

claims.quote: It is recommended, but not required, that implementations support exact integers and exact rationals of practically unlimited size and precision

an implementation that uses IEEE binary double-precision floating-point numbers to represent all its inexact real numbers may also support a practically unbounded range of exact integers and rationals

says.covers: integers kept exact past two to the 53rd

claims.where: 6.2.3 Implementation restrictions (an example of what an implementation may do)

claims.quote: If the written representation of a number has no exactness prefix, the constant is inexact if it contains a decimal point or an exponent.
claims.where: 6.2.5 Syntax of numerical constants (so 0.1 reads inexact)

claims.quote: A numerical constant can be specified to be either exact or inexact by a prefix.

says.covers: decimal literals read as exact

claims.where: 6.2.5 Syntax of numerical constants (#e for exact, #i for inexact)

claims.quote: The implementation approach of converting all arguments to inexact numbers if any argument is inexact is not transitive.

claims.quote: each number is also either an exact number or an inexact number
The precision and size of exact numbers is limited only by available memory (and the precision of operations that can produce irrational numbers).

claims.quote: In particular, adding, multiplying, subtracting, and dividing exact numbers always produces an exact result.
